meta.title: How devhost reports operations and problems: proposed

frontend.label: UI step where the work started

nodes.label: Any write or its key
nodes.explanation: Every write a page sends starts the same way: a row's Restart, Restart Changed with its badge icon and Alt+Ctrl+R, Start, Restart Stack, Switch and Restart Stack, Return to Configured Worktree, Save, and Send in the Disable Reloads popover (WORD-11). The operation's name is the label of the control or command that started it, the same on every surface (MENU-6, WORD-2); a key or an icon acts on the set its control names, and its outcome names that set: Alt+Ctrl+R is Restart Changed, on 'api, web' when they are changed, else on the page's own service, 'docs' on the docs page (SEL-1, SEL-2, O4). Writes that ask first ask in their own flow's surface (REV-1); this flow adds no question, and no question ever sits in a notice (REV-4, SURF-2). A key whose action is unavailable reports why in a neutral notice, 'Restart Changed did not run: Restart Stack is running · 3 of 6 started', which closes after O14's calibrated reading time and stays in the log (MENU-3, HOLD-3, WORD-7, O14, O53). Today each control keeps its own progress and error; one model replaces them (notices-and-feedback-03).

sources.label: Replaces: row Restart's shared error
Replaces: Restart Stack's own pending, error
Replaces: the picker's own error

nodes.label: Control keeps focus
nodes.explanation: The pressed control keeps focus as the busy control, aria-busy and aria-disabled, never disabled, its label naming what runs: 'Restarting api…', 'Restarting Stack · 2 of 6 started' (KEY-11, FB-9, WORD-4), drawn with toolbar-shell's unavailable and busy Button state. The request carries an operationId, a lowercase UUID the page generates, and the page ID of this page load; the page-side operation store keeps each ID the tab sent in sessionStorage, so only this tab treats the operation as its own and a reload in the middle keeps following it (ACT-1, CC-37). The announcer says the start once, in its polite region: 'Restarting api' (FB-9). Each control's own key starts it; this step adds no key.

sources.label: Replaces: row Restart disabled while it runs
Replaces: Restart Stack disabled while it runs

nodes.label: Operation record
nodes.explanation: Every write route takes the operationId and the page ID and answers 202 Accepted with the operation record before the operation runs: its ID, kind, targets, origin (a page with its page ID and hostname, the CLI, an agent with its DEVHOST_CHAT_SESSION conversation, or the watcher with the changed file), each target's step and outcome with cause and evidence, the work it ended, and its start and end times (ACT-1, CC-37). It streams on /__devhost__/ws/health at least once a second while it runs and stays until the next operation of the same kind on the same target; a failed outcome stays until dismissed via POST /__devhost__/operations/<id>/dismiss or superseded. A lost response is read from the record by its ID, and a repeated ID returns the record and runs nothing again (REV-12); no surface infers a result by counting reloads or health messages. services-panel ships it first for restart-service, restart-stack, start-service and stop-service; this flow requires it for worktrees POST, config/save, disk reloads and the Disable Reloads send. One operation at a time per stack stays.

sources.label: Reuses: name checks, then stop and start each
Reuses: Restart Stack as one change
Replaces: POST with no operation ID

nodes.label: Progress in one place
nodes.explanation: While the surface that started the operation is open, it shows each target's step (queued, stopping, starting, 'health check 2 s of 30 s', running, failed), updated at least once a second, and the busy control's elapsed time (FB-1, ACT-3, STATE-1). Whenever no open surface on the page shows it, because its panel closed (Escape, a click outside, Tab past its last control: KEY-7, KEY-8) or it started in another tab, the terminal, an agent or a file saved on disk, the notice stack shows one activity line (including in one-line form beside the collapsed badge), 'Restart Stack · 2 of 6 started · 5 s', ending with its origin when it came from elsewhere, '· from the terminal' (FB-1, WORD-4, ACT-1). It has no Dismiss; its outcome replaces it (FB-2). Touched rows show restarting, starting or stopping on every surface and the others keep their state; starting one service never draws running ones as down (ACT-3, ACT-4, SEL-7). Ticking text sits outside every live region (FB-9). Every page's stream stays open through Restart Stack and Start (services-panel's backend), so no all-down second ends them (services-panel-2-04, stack-scale-06).

sources.label: Replaces: dot states with no step or time
Replaces: 'Switching and restarting stack…'

nodes.label: One outcome where it ran
nodes.explanation: The outcome replaces progress in place: in its open surface, else as an outcome notice in place of the activity line, never both (FB-2). It names the operation in past tense, targets, changes and duration: 'Restarted Acme Shop · 6 of 6 running · new automatic ports for api and web · 14 s' (FB-3, WORD-4, WORD-5). It certifies end state (FB-5) and names ended work (FB-4). A success closes after calibrated reading time (1.5 s + 0.3 s/word, 4-15 s; Undo 4 s) when pointer and focus leave and the page is visible, pausing before counting only if it arrived while document.hasFocus() was false (FB-6, O14, O53); logged outcomes say 'also in the log' while unlogged ones omit it (FB-7). Each outcome announces once, politely (FB-9, keyboard-and-screen-reader-02). Another origin appends its source and shows only on failure or the page's service (SEL-3). After a reload it caused or a turn-end reload ('Reloaded to show Claude Code's change', O57), the next page reads it once (ACT-1, KEY-6); failed Restart Stack or switch reports its rollback (UNDO-1).

sources.label: Replaces: success clears the button
Replaces: applied once a reload is counted
Replaces: a switch reloads, says nothing

nodes.label: Same line in terminal
nodes.explanation: Every operation on a running stack, from any origin, prints one outcome line in the stack's terminal and in its per-manifest log: the sentence the page shows, built from the record by the outcome sentence builders' Rust counterpart in apps/devhost/src/cliout.rs (FB-10, FB-7, WORD-4, WORD-9, CC-22). 'Restarted api · 2.6 s · from a page on shop.localhost' now follows 'restarting service: api'; a fix saved from the Configuration window prints 'Applied devhost.toml: restarted web (changed) · 6 of 6 running · 1.2 s', so the terminal never ends on a rejection already fixed (notices-and-feedback-03). Page-started operations use '· from a page on <hostname>' in the terminal and log (WORD-4). The URL list prints at the first start and on request (devhost stack info, short alias devhost status, O62), never after each action (FB-10). Every stack writes its log, a foreground one included, and the pinned log panel offers devhost's own lines (CC-21; log-minimap). Agent output keeps a failure on one devhost: ERR: line, and agents read the last outcome from devhost stack info / devhost status and the log (FB-11, CC-23, O62).

sources.label: Replaces: 'restarting service:', no end line
Replaces: URL list after every change
Replaces: 'configuration reload rejected'

nodes.label: Another tab, CLI, agent
nodes.sublabel: or a file saved on disk
nodes.explanation: An operation can start where this page sees no press: another tab, the terminal, an agent, or a manifest file saved on disk. Its record carries its origin as far as the backend can see it: each page sends its page ID, the CLI marks its requests, an agent devhost started runs with DEVHOST_CHAT_SESSION, and the watcher cannot tell an editor's save from an agent's edit, so it reads 'after devhost.toml changed on disk' (ACT-1, WORD-4). Every open page shows its activity line and draws its rows' transitions (FB-1, ACT-3); its outcome reaches a page as a notice only when it failed or touched the page's own service, and always as a log line (FB-2, FB-7). When an editor save arrives while the browser window is unfocused, O53 pauses its notice countdown until focus returns.

sources.label: Reuses: a saved manifest file reloads

nodes.label: Failure stays in place
nodes.explanation: A failure leads with the target and what happened, then the cause, the evidence and where to fix it: 'api exited with code 1 at 14:02 before its health check', its last lines, the probe or a port's holder (FAIL-2, FAIL-3, WORD-7). It stays in its surface, and as a failure notice once that closes, until Dismiss or the same operation succeeds; stream messages, reconnects and reloads never remove it (FB-6, ACT-1). Focus stays on the control, which the failure describes; the assertive region says it once and the tab title prefixes until cleared (KEY-11, FB-9, O16). It leads with MENU-5's action (Copy and Copy Error when the config editor is off, O51). An unreadable response never shows: the shared request helper makes one sentence ('Acme Shop is not running…', or 'Sign in with passkey or pair this browser to use devhost here' on a 403 from an unauthenticated remote browser, O36, HOLD-7), with the original behind Copy Error (FAIL-2; notices-and-feedback-01, journey-new-project-02). A partial result counts every target, and a rollback names what it restored (FAIL-1, UNDO-1). Repeats update a count (FAIL-4); a deliberate stop is neutral (FAIL-5); a stale write is refused (REV-13).

sources.label: Replaces: each status message clears the error
Replaces: any non-JSON body as the error
Replaces: any non-2xx body as the message

nodes.label: A condition starts
nodes.explanation: A condition is a state that lasts until something changes it. Each comes from the published state, worded by the flow that owns it: the page's service or a dependency exited, its crash view minimized (startup-and-recovery); a manifest file or the devhost config file not applied (manifest-hot-reload); a repository blocked by its worktree (worktree-switch, WORD-11; external services never block switches, O7); an external service not reachable (services-panel); an agent waiting for the person in chat or a terminal, or chat turned off with conversations still running (agent-chat, running-agents); a held or blocked reload (reload-control); the lost connection or a single closed command-mode serve port (this flow, serve-command-05). This flow owns their form, order, lifetime, tab-title prefix and announcements (ACT-7, O16).

nodes.label: Conditions in one stack
nodes.explanation: Each condition is one notice while it lasts, starting and ending with the published state and clearing with its cause, never by a timer or reload (ACT-7), leading with MENU-5's action (Answer for chat waiting; Dismiss alone for terminal waiting). Order: what needs the person or blocks writes, then activity lines, then other conditions, then successes, newest first; three show, the rest fold into 2 More / Show Fewer (FB-8). The stack sits beside the bar, uncovered by panels, chat or Configuration, adapting down to 320 CSS px phone width with >=24 px targets (SURF-1, CC-1, SURF-9, O8). Waiting agents and failures prefix app and devhost tab titles until cleared (ACT-7, O16). Dismissed conditions leave a control marker (SURF-8, UNDO-3); collapsed, conditions, failures and activity lines keep one-line forms while only successes stay in the log (FB-1). Notices carry no live role (Alert drops role=alert): the announcer speaks once per start and end, inside the topmost modal too (FB-9). Arrivals never take focus, and Escape dismisses nothing (KEY-6, KEY-8).

sources.label: Replaces: three notices with no order
Replaces: role=alert on every notice

nodes.label: devhost stop, caddy stop
nodes.explanation: A page loses its stack's stream when the stack stops (devhost stop from a terminal or an agent, Ctrl-C, the idle timeout, a replacement by devhost stack restart, devhost restart or devhost upgrade under O18, or a stop from another stack's page), when devhost caddy stop takes the shared proxy away, when proxy-settings moves the HTTPS port, or when a single secondary HTTP port closes in a multi-port command-mode devhost serve -- <cmd> session while sibling ports stay healthy (serve-command-05). devhost never opens a browser or starts a stack from the page: its notices offer commands to copy or active URLs to open (owner rule, ACT-10).

nodes.label: Stopping, final message
nodes.explanation: The shutdown, which today drops the control server before it stops services, keeps it up until they stopped (O30's 30 s allowance) and first publishes the stack's stopping state with the count stopped, so pages show 'Stopping Acme Shop · 3 of 6 stopped' instead of 6 of 6 running (ACT-3, WORD-4). After services stop or the allowance runs out, it sends stack-ended on /__devhost__/ws/health with reason, by, at, folder, start command, survivors, ended conversations and replacedBy (command, time, new run's stack ID; never a PID, R7-99), then closes with 1001 (HOLD-2, ACT-10, ACT-11, CC-26). devhost caddy stop sends proxy-stopping first; proxy-settings sends listeners-moving with each listener's old and new address before Caddy moves, then listeners-moved or listeners-failed (FB-13). For multi-port command-mode serve sessions, refresh_command_routes sends port-closed with the closed port and remaining active URLs before removing that port's Caddy route and closes cleanly (serve-command-05). openReconnectingWebSocket.ts passes the close event and final message to its handler; a silent drop probes once to tell a stopped stack from an unreachable proxy.

sources.label: Replaces: control server stops before services
Reuses: streams close with a reason

nodes.label: Lost connection: unknown
nodes.explanation: From the moment the stream closes, every write on the page (Restart, Restart Changed and its key, Start, Restart Stack, switches, Stop Stack, Save, chat Send, Disable Reloads' Send) is unavailable with one reason, said once in this notice and in each open panel's status line and given to each control as its description (HOLD-2, HOLD-1, MENU-3); every service keeps its last known state as unknown, 'last seen 16:24', never down (ACT-5, CC-26, WORD-6). The reason names the cause: 'Acme Shop stopped at 16:24 by devhost stop. Start it with devhost start in ~/acme' with Copy; '… but api still runs (PID 4242, port 5173)'; 'devhost's proxy is not reachable. Start it with devhost caddy start'; 'Moving to port 4443', then 'Moved to https://shop.localhost:4443/' with Open once every listener answers (FB-13); for a single closed command-mode serve port, 'Port 4002 closed · demoapp still runs on https://demoapp.localhost' with Open, never a false 0/3 outage (serve-command-05); else 'Lost connection to devhost; retrying' with Retry Now. Stopped is read only from the final message (ACT-11). It has no Dismiss; drafts, page context and queued operations stay (UNDO-2, SEL-7).

sources.label: Replaces: disconnect marks every service down
Replaces: unknown drawn as status false
Replaces: close code and reason dropped

nodes.label: Connected again · 6 of 6
nodes.explanation: The page retries with today's back-off, 1 s doubling to 10 s, and Retry Now tries at once (HOLD-2). After a port move or a closed command-mode port (serve-command-05), Open goes to the new or remaining active URL and the page stops retrying the dead hostname (proxy-settings-03). When the stream returns, states update in place, every write is available again without a reload and nothing it blocked is replayed (HOLD-1, REV-12); the page says once, politely (without 'also in the log', O14), 'Connected again · 6 of 6 running', or after a replacement 'Connected again · Acme Shop was replaced by devhost restart at 14:02 · 6 of 6 running', once the stream carries the stack ID replacedBy named (ACT-5, ACT-10, WORD-4, O18, R7-99). The notices the outage raised clear with it; a reload held meanwhile clears when the page's service still runs the process it ran at load, else stays as Reload blocked; failures the record keeps stay (ACT-7, FB-6). A tab left open on a stopped stack keeps its stopped notice and reconnects when the stack starts again.

cards.title: What changes versus today
items: Removed: the toolbar-wide error that each status message clears; role=alert on every notice; a lost connection drawn as every service down and false 0/3 outages on a single closed command-mode port (serve-command-05); response bodies, markup and raw Rust error chains or transport errors as error text; Open in Editor fallback (O51); 6 of 6 running through a shutdown; the silent reconnection; a Reload blocked that outlives its outage; the URL list after every change; 'Saved and applied.' and 'configuration reload rejected' as words

Merged: the toolbar-wide error, Restart Stack's and Restart Changed's own errors, the Worktrees picker's notice and the Configuration window's result strip into one outcome model, one record and one notice stack; a stopped stack, a stopped proxy, a moved port, a closed command-mode port and an unexplained drop into one lost connection that names its cause

New: the notice stack component (failure, condition, activity, success, neutral) with 320 px phone layout (O8); calibrated reading time (1.5 s + 0.3 s/word, 4-15 s; Undo 4 s, O14) and unfocused-arrival pause via document.hasFocus() (O53); app and devhost tab-title prefixing for waiting agents and failures (O16); turn-end reload outcome notice (O57); targeted port-closed notice with active URLs (serve-command-05); the announcer; activity lines; outcome notices with origin; 2 More and Show Fewer; dismissal markers and collapsed one-line forms; page-side operation store; shared request helper with O36 unauthenticated copy; Retry Now and 'Connected again'; stopping state and final message; terminal/log outcome line and foreground log

Changed: Alert is a group named by its sentence, not role=alert; a lost connection is unknown, never down (CC-26); openReconnectingWebSocket.ts passes the close event and final message (including port-closed); control errors are sentences; Reload blocked clears with its cause; every write carries an operationId and gets 202 Accepted (CC-37); a switch stores its ID before the reload; every stack writes its log (CC-21); the control server stays up until services stop; inspection uses devhost stack info / devhost status (O62)

Kept: progress where the operation started, now with steps and time; colliding controls unavailable, now naming the running operation; reconnecting after 1 s, doubling to 10 s; a save reported only once applied, now from the reload that read it; Copy on failures and Edit on a file not applied; a log line per completed change, now per operation; Reload on a held reload; a rejected reload keeps the accepted manifest and blocks nothing; saves apply without a question; devhost's own reloads never held; readouts hidden while disconnected; devhost never opens a browser; no chat delivery claimed or resent; a failed service leaves the rest running; human and agent output differ by design

Failures kept, in one sentence: notices-and-feedback-01, journey-new-project-02
Conditions and the announcer: keyboard-and-screen-reader-02

Single closed command-mode port: serve-command-05 (targeted port-closed notice over WebSocket instead of false 0/3 outage)

Slices here, the rest elsewhere: journey-new-project-02 and services-panel-2-04 (services-panel); notices-and-feedback-01 (config-editor, services-panel); notices-and-feedback-03 (toolbar-shell); proxy-settings-03 (proxy-settings); serve-command-05 (serve-folder)
Related, not covered: error-pages-02 (P1, startup-and-recovery), which keeps a failed Restart Stack's outcome in the crash view; this flow's record keeps that failure until it is handled

cards.title: Backend work
items: Operation record for every write in apps/devhost/src/devtools/server.rs and streams.rs: operationId and page ID, 202 Accepted with the record, streamed at least once a second, kept until the next operation of its kind, a failure until handled; a repeated ID runs nothing (CC-37; services-panel ships its first routes)
POST /__devhost__/operations/<id>/dismiss (gated under O36) marks a failure handled for every page of the stack (CC-37)

The stream's final message before it closes: stack-ended with reason, by, at, folder, start command, survivors, ended conversations and replacedBy (command, time, new stack ID); proxy-stopping from devhost caddy stop; listeners-moving, then listeners-moved or listeners-failed, from proxy-settings (FB-13); port-closed from apps/devhost/src/services/stack/command.rs with remaining activeUrls before removing a closed command-mode port route (CC-26, serve-command-05)
Stopping published before services stop, with the count stopped, coordinated with O30 parallel shutdown (CC-26)
Streams stay open across Restart Stack and Start: services-panel's backend, relied on here

One outcome line per operation in the terminal and the per-manifest log, built in apps/devhost/src/cliout.rs with page origin '· from a page on <hostname>'; a foreground stack writes its log; failure lines carry ERR: (CC-21, CC-22, CC-23)
Each service's launch time in the published state tells whether a held reload is still needed (services-panel's state; no new field)

cards.title: Contract changes
items: CC-26: a lost connection is unknown, never down, with every write unavailable and its reason
CC-37: operationId, 202 Accepted, failure dismissal and the record on the health stream (services-panel lands its routes; this flow reads and dismisses from it)
CC-21: every stack writes its per-manifest log, a foreground one included
CC-22: one outcome line for every operation on a running stack (this flow); stop and ready lines (stack-run-stop); the reload line (manifest-hot-reload)

CC-23: an agent-output error is one devhost: ERR: line, and failure lines in the log carry ERR: (extending devhost stack info with alias devhost status, plus reload and logs, are stack-run-stop's, O62)
CC-1: no devhost surface covers the notice stack (toolbar-shell lands it)

guides/devtools.md gains a section on the notice stack covering O8 phone layout, O14/O53 durations and unfocused pause, O16 tab-title prefix, O57 turn-end reload, lost connection and command-mode port-closed notices
